This application is filed by the applicants-Corporation under Section 5 of the Indian Limitation Act, 1963, seeking condonation of delay of 247 days in filing this appeal challenging the order dt. 28.07.2022 passed by the learned Single Judge in CWPOA no.4365 of 2019.

2) In the application filed seeking condonation of delay, it is cryptically stated the delay in filing the appeal was occasioned due to the fact that the file had to be routed through various channels which took considerable time, that it was ultimately in April, 2023 sent to the present counsel who was engaged to file the appeal and he thus filed the appeal on 18.04.2023.
It is stated that the delay in filing the appeal is not intentional or deliberate and the delay may be condoned.

3) Reply was filed by the respondents to the said application opposing the .

sentences.text: 4) Thereafter, rejoinder is filed by the applicants-Corporation, elaborating on the reasons for the delay in filing the appeal and referring to certain judgments which will be discussed hereafter.

of 5) The following is, however, stated in the rejoinder, which is required to be noted:-
rt

"At the same time the appellant corporation concedes that the state or it's instrumentalities/corporations are required to file any appeal with due promptness and well within the prescribed period of limitation as Limitation act applies equally to the state at par with an individual but most respectfully sometimes as has happened in the present case in case of Public corporations, Public bodies or even state a collective decision is required to be taken and therefore when a file has to be processed/routed through various number of channels some time is consumed.
Sometimes the staff though is required to be very proactive and alert does not speed up the things as required due to which finally some delay occurs.

But the appellant corporation being the responsible corporation is well aware of it's responsibilities and is taking steps that the delay in filing in any appeal is either eliminated or at least be minimized."
Thus the appellants were clearly aware that they should have acted with promptitude and filed the appeal within the time prescribed by law.

6) In addition thereto, it is stated that the respondent was taking undue benefit of pure hyper technicalities; that the issue involved in the case affects large number of cases; that the respondent tried to influence the .
Corporation through a U.O. Note of the Hon'ble Speaker (which is not filed); that it was observed in the Noting File that the matter earlier could not be considered in time, firstly, due to non-receipt of judgment in time and then because it had to be processed through various channels.
of 7) Certain contentions on the merits of the case were also raised.
8) We have noted the contentions of the parties.

sentences.text:
We have already extracted the reasons as mentioned in the "better affidavit"
sworn by Mr. Aparajeet Pattanayak, SSRM, Air Mail Sorting Division, New Delhi.

It is relevant to note that in the said affidavit, the Department has itself mentioned and is aware of the date of the judgment of the Division Bench of the High Court in Office of the Chief Postmaster v.
Living Media India Ltd. as 11.09.2009.

sentences.text: Even according to the deponent, their counsel had applied for the certified copy of the said judgment only on 08.01.2010 and the same was received by the Department on the very same day.
There is no explanation for not applying for certified copy of the impugned judgment on 11.09.2009 or at least within a reasonable time.
The fact remains that the certified copy was applied only on 08.01.2010, i.e. after a period of nearly four months.

26. In spite of affording another opportunity to file better affidavit by placing adequate material, neither the Department nor the person in-charge has filed any explanation for not applying the certified copy within the prescribed period.

The other dates mentioned in the affidavit which we have already (2012) 3 SCC 563 extracted, clearly show that there was delay at every stage and except mentioning the dates of receipt of the file and the decision taken, there is no explanation as to why such delay had occasioned.

Though it was stated by the Department that the delay was due to unavoidable circumstances and genuine difficulties, the fact remains that from day one the Department or the .
person/persons concerned have not evinced diligence in prosecuting the matter to this Court by taking appropriate steps.

27. It is not in dispute that the person(s) concerned were well aware or conversant with the issues involved including the prescribed period of limitation for taking up the matter by way of filing a special leave petition in this Court.
They cannot claim that they have a separate period of limitation of when the Department was possessed with competent persons familiar with court proceedings.

In the absence of plausible and acceptable explanation, we are posing a question why the delay is to be condoned mechanically merely because the Government or a wing of the Government is a party before us.
rt 28.

Though we are conscious of the fact that in a matter of condonation of delay when there was no gross negligence or deliberate inaction or lack of bona fides, a liberal concession has to be adopted to advance substantial justice, we are of the view that in the facts and circumstances, the Department cannot take advantage of various earlier decisions.
The claim on account of impersonal machinery and inherited bureaucratic methodology of making several notes cannot be accepted in view of the modern technologies being used and available.
The law of limitation undoubtedly binds everybody, including the Government."

We shall now discuss the judgment cited by the counsel for the applicants:-
(a) The decision in Delhi Development Authority Vs. Jagan Singh & Others, Civil Appeal no.4335 of 2023, decided on 13.07.2023.

entities.text: Delhi Development Authority Vs. Jagan Singh & Others, Civil Appeal no.4335 of 2023
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: of The said appeal arose out of an order passed by the High Court allowing a Writ Petition which had been challenged in the Supreme Court rt with a delay of 1231 days.

Though it was observed by the Supreme Court that the application for condonation of delay was drafted casually in that case, the Bench had decided to adopt the justice-oriented and liberal approach and condoned the delay.

A reading of the said judgment indicates that the Delhi High Court had allowed a Writ petition holding that acquisition proceedings were deemed to have lapsed in view of sub-Section 2 of Section 24 of the 2013 Act, placing reliance on the judgment of the Pune Municipal Corporation & Another vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & others7.

entities.text: Pune Municipal Corporation & Another vs. Harakchand Misirimal Solanki & others7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Afterwards, the said judgment in Pune Municipal Corporation & Another was overruled by the Supreme (2021) 11 SCC 557 (2022) 9 SCC 263 (2022) 9 SCC 266 (2014) 3 SCC 183 Court on 06.03.2020 in Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal &
others8.

entities.text:
Indore Development Authority vs. Manoharlal &
others8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Supreme Court, therefore, first decided that the proceedings for .
acquisition would not lapse; and that sub-Section (2) of Section 24 of the 2013 Act would have no application because possession of the acquired land was already taken on 19.01.2006 though compensation had not been paid.
It therefore condoned the delay as acquired land had already been of utilized for a public purpose for a Metro Depot.

While observing that it was not influenced by the fact that the decision on which the impugned judgment rt was based had been overruled and though the SLP had been filed 2 years 3 days after the date of decision of the Supreme Court in Indore Development Authority (supra-8), it held that the Supreme Court had repeatedly taken a view that liberal and justice-oriented approach needs to be adopted in the matters of condonation of delay, so that substantive rights of parties are not defeated only on the ground of delay.

sentences.text: We may point out that the decision in Postmaster General and others (supra-1) and the other judgments referred to above applying it have neither been adverted to nor considered and applied by the Supreme Court in the above case.
May be in the facts & circumstances in Delhi Development Authority, the Supreme Court thought it fit to condone the delay.
However, we prefer to (2020) 8 SCC 129 follow the judgment in Postmaster General and others (supra-1) and the other cases which followed it.

(b) The next judgment cited by the counsel for the applicants is decision of the .
Supreme Court rendered on 24.07.2023 in Civil Appeal no.4628 of 2023.
In this case the delay was only 52 days in filing the appeal.

So the Court observed that parties were litigating with regard to rights over immovable property and substantive rights were to be decided between the of parties, and the High Court was in error in refusing to condone the said period of delay in filing the first appeal before the Appellate Court.
Also, in that rt case neither the State nor an instrumentality of the State was a party.
Thus the said decision is distinguishable and it cannot be applied to the instant case since the delay on its part is 212 days, for which no valid reason has been furnished by the applicants.

(c) Counsel for the applicants relied on the judgment of the Supreme Court in Sheo Raj Singh (deceased) through LRs & Others Vs. Union of India & Another, Civil Appeal no.5867 of 2015 dt.
09.10.2023.

entities.text: LRs & Others Vs. Union of India & Another, Civil Appeal no.5867 of 2015
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Sheo Raj Singh, the High Court had condoned the delay of 479 days in filing a Land Acquisition Appeal in the High Court and the explanation offered found favour with the Supreme Court.

In that case, the Supreme Court observed that it was not hearing an application for condonation of delay,
but was sitting in appeal over discretionary exercise of the High Court granting the prayer for condonation of delay; in the case of the former, whether to condone or not, would be the only question, whereas in the latter, whether there has been proper exercise of discretion in favour of grant of prayer for condonation, would be the question; and .
the law was well settled that a Court of appeal should not ordinarily interfere with the discretionary exercise by the Courts below, and that the appellate power should be exercised only when the order challenged in appeal is clearly wrong and not when it is merely not right.

of The said decision therefore cannot help the applicants since in the instant application, this Court has to consider the question whether rt sufficient cause has been shown to condone the period of delay.
It is not considering an order passed by a subordinate forum condoning the delay or refusing to condone it.

12) In the instant case, we may point out that the judgment of the learned Single Judge was delivered on 28.07.2022, but application for certified copy of the same was filed on 14.02.2023, six Himachal Road Transport Corporation & ... vs Malkiat Singh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59986072/
5 & half (6 ) months after the judgment was pronounced; and after the copy of the judgment was delivered on 24.03.2023, the appeal was filed on 18.04.2023.
No explanation is offered by the applicants why application for certified copy could not be filed in the 6  months period between 28.07.2022 to 14.02.2023.

13) We are therefore of the opinion that the applicants-Corporation had been totally negligent in pursuing the remedy of appeal against the order of the learned Single Judge, that the period of delay being inordinate, and sufficient cause not having been shown for condoning the said period of delay,
this application deserves to be dismissed.

Accordingly, this .
application is dismissed.
14) Consequently, the appeal (Filing No.LPA/9751/2023) is also dismissed.
